node: Data-center power delivery, grid interconnection, transformers, switchgear, and thermal infrastructure
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion found a compact direct-exposure universe around the AI data-center power stack. The strongest underfollowed candidates are not GPU or hyperscaler names, but firms tied to medium-voltage switchgear, dry-type transformers, liquid-cooling/power distribution components, and regional utility service territories where binding data-center load contracts are turning AI demand into rate-base or backlog signals. This is a research universe only, not a recommendation list. POWL and HMDPF are the cleanest equipment bottleneck candidates; NVT is a larger, more visible power-and-cooling component platform; EVRG is a regulated utility/load-growth candidate that needs tariff, capex, and customer-credit verification. Layer 1B expands the underfollowed universe around AI data-center physical infrastructure. The strongest directly evidenced small/mid-cap discovery candidate is Powell Industries, where official 2026 disclosures show record backlog and a post-quarter data-center order above $400 million. AAON is a cooling-infrastructure candidate with official evidence of BASX data-center cooling demand and record backlog. nVent is larger and increasingly recognized, but remains useful as a narrow electrical-connection/protection and liquid-cooling component supplier rather than a generic AI name. AEP is included as a regulated-asset reference/discovery bridge: it is not small-cap, but its utility territory and large-load commitments make it a demand-anchor and interconnection-cost pass-through monitor for the node. No trading recommendation is implied. Layer 1B expansion fou
